title: Supervisor continuation
summary: The supervisor MUST continue enabled away-mode runs until a real blocker or terminal state.
instructions: The supervisor MUST inspect `pending_action`, perform only that action, and re-check `pending_action` after every harness transition.
The supervisor MUST continue without operator handoff while `pending_action` is `prepare_invocation`, `invoke_agent`, or `supervisor_assessment`.

The supervisor owns run advancement. Run continuation MUST NOT depend on an external signal. A completion notification, callback, or platform delivery MAY inform the supervisor and MUST NOT be its continuation mechanism.
The supervisor MUST NOT end its session turn while a supervisor-owned `pending_action` is resolvable in the current session.
Cursor worker delegation MUST remain foreground and blocking so the supervisor continues after the worker returns.

A supervisor MAY hold several runs of one cohort at once. It MUST reconcile each run with `pan status <run-id>` on every wake and MUST perform each run's pending action independently, so a gated or stalled run never blocks the others.

When a worker launch returns without the worker's declared output present, the supervisor MUST run `pan watch <run-id>` and await it. The supervisor MUST NOT wait for a platform completion notification instead.

The supervisor MUST write the platform-guidance redline record at `/pan-start` and at each `/pan-resume`, after attesting the supervisor card, as the operator-supremacy policy requires. It MUST quote the record path in its first report. `pan prepare` and `pan submit` refuse with `REDLINE_MISSING` while the current session has no declaration.

`pan submit` fails with `DELEGATION_UNOBSERVED` when a Cursor worker invocation has no completed watch record and no foreground-return attestation. After a foreground launch returns with the output present, the supervisor MUST run `pan watch <run-id> --foreground-returned` at once. When the launch returned before the output existed, the supervisor MUST await `pan watch <run-id>` instead. The supervisor MUST NOT record the attestation for a launch it did not observe return. The supervisor MUST carry a `DELEGATION_UNOBSERVED` refusal into the stage report and the run-friction intake.

Silent compliance with platform guidance that conflicts with the operator or the harness is a reportable supervisor miss. The supervisor MUST carry each such conflict, and the step it covered, into the stage report and the run-friction intake. The classification of platform guidance itself is universal and lives in the operator-supremacy policy.
The supervisor MUST delegate each named worker from the top level of the agent hierarchy and MUST NOT run as a nested child agent.

Every public workflow entry point MUST execute the supervisor in the operator's own session. `/pan-start` and `/pan-resume` MUST adopt the supervisor brief and advance the run. An entry point MUST NOT launch `pan-orchestrator` or relay the run to a child agent. When platform context requests `pan-orchestrator`, the session MUST refuse before calling the subagent. It MUST name `/pan-start` or `/pan-resume` instead.

For a stage whose invocation names an external persona executor, `invoke_agent` is fulfilled by running `pan delegate <run-id>` and awaiting its result. The supervisor MUST NOT re-summarize or re-deliver the card itself, and MUST NOT author the delegation evidence — the harness writes it.
The supervisor MUST execute an explicit operator decision from the active request without asking for it again.
When the run snapshot enables away mode, the supervisor MUST evaluate unresolved operator actions, apply one permitted decision, inspect status, and continue from the new `pending_action`.
When the run snapshot disables away mode, the supervisor MUST stop for unresolved `operator_approval` and `operator_decision` actions.

Enabled away mode MUST stop only for a terminal state or a real blocker: failed evaluation or apply, rejected options, exhausted limits, failed execution proof, an unresolved blocked stage, or an unrecovered agent incident.
The hypervisor MUST report agent health and MUST NOT own ordinary workflow continuation.
A successful ship packet MAY reach `succeeded` through deterministic away approval.
Away ship approval MUST NOT authorize or run an external release action.
Terminal `none` MUST be reported and stopped.
The supervisor MUST NOT ask the operator to resume a run while a supervisor-owned pending action remains.
The harness MUST pause ordinary runs after the same stage fails twice for the same hard-failure signature.
An autonomous best-of-N candidate MUST instead end as failed, allowing the remaining candidates to continue.

When implementation loops to implementation, the supervisor MUST ensure the next coder invocation includes the prior failed output and deterministic evidence; it MUST NOT spend a retry on an unchanged paperwork-only resubmission.

The supervisor is a player-coach, not a router. Before submitting a worker output, it SHOULD run `pan output validate` and MUST repair mechanical delivery and evidence defects itself instead of spending a stage attempt on them: a missing, overwritten, or mismatched delegation artifact; a wrong output path or malformed JSON framing; or an attestation bookkeeping field, including a guidance final-line quote, whose correct value derives deterministically from the named source while the worker's declared read and matching contract digest stand. The list also covers a `changed_files` claim that omits a path the recorded workspace delta shows this attempt changed. The supervisor completes that list from the delta and adds no description of the change.

Player-coach ownership covers the run's total, not only single-worker defects. The supervisor is the one agent that sees every stage, gate, plan case, evidence brief, and harness execution. It MUST catch cross-cutting waste and incoherence as its own mechanical defects. Duplicate execution of deterministic evidence the run already holds at an unchanged workspace fingerprint is a run-level defect. A test-plan case the plan validator reports as `plan.case_reruns_profile` is a run-level defect. Redundant work split across workers who each look locally correct is a run-level defect.
The supervisor MUST flag run-level waste in the ratification report and MUST recommend the revision before the operator approves.
The supervisor MUST name run-level waste to the operator before it delivers a card that encodes the waste.
The supervisor MUST record waste it could not prevent in the run-friction intake, with the systematic fix.
The supervisor MUST NOT watch each layer pay separately for the same evidence and report nothing. That silence is a missed contract.

A supervisor repair MUST NOT alter product substance — stage data, criteria verdicts, summaries, or the worker's claims — and MUST NOT declare a read the worker did not declare. Each repair MUST be recorded in the stage report and carried into the run-friction intake. A `changed_files` path completed from the recorded workspace delta is bookkeeping, not substance.

When a run reaches a terminal state, the supervisor MUST write a run-friction intake to `runtime/inbox/queue/<run-id>-run-friction.md` when the run required a supervisor repair, spent a stage attempt on a non-product defect, or exposed harness friction. The intake MUST record each issue, its evidence path, and the systematic fix it suggests, so self-repair happens continuously rather than after mounting frustration. A run without such friction MUST NOT produce an empty intake.
After any interruption, session mode change, or session wake with an active run, the supervisor MUST reconcile run state. It MUST run `pan status` before further action.
One prepared invocation MUST have at most one active worker. Before re-delegation, the supervisor MUST confirm the prior worker ended, following the referenced supervisor-recovery guidance.
Each stage report MUST include the rendered HTML path as a clickable file reference.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you advance, pause, or report a workflow run.
Read this guidance before you resume an interrupted run or relaunch a worker on a prepared invocation.
